questions.question_text:
In the given text, the blanks are numbered (i)−(iv). Select the best match for all the
blanks.
Steve was advised to keep his head (i) before heading (ii) to bat;
for, while he had a head (iii) batting, he could only do so with a cool head
s (iv) his shoulders.
questions.subtopic: Vocabulary: words, idioms, and phrases in context
questions.explaination: 'Keep one's head down' means to stay focused and avoid trouble. 'Heading out' means going forth/departing. Having a 'head for' an activity signifies natural aptitude for it, and having a cool 'head on' one's shoulders means remaining calm and composed.

questions.question_text:
A rectangular paper sheet of dimensions 54 cm × 4 cm is taken. The two longer
edges of the sheet are joined together to create a cylindrical tube. A cube whose
surface area is equal to the area of the sheet is also taken.
Then, the ratio of the volume of the cylindrical tube to the volume of the cube is
questions.explaination: Joining the longer edges ($54\text{ cm}$) creates a cylinder with height $h = 54\text{ cm}$ and circumference $2\pi r = 4\text{ cm} \implies r = \frac{2}{\pi}$, giving volume $V_{\text{cyl}} = \pi r^2 h = \frac{216}{\pi}$. The sheet area is $54 \times 4 = 216\text{ cm}^2$. A cube with surface area $6a^2 = 216$ has edge $a = 6\text{ cm}$ and volume $V_{\text{cube}} = 6^3 = 216$. Thus $\frac{V_{\text{cyl}}}{V_{\text{cube}}} = \frac{216/\pi}{216} = \frac{1}{\pi}$.

questions.question_text:
A rectangular paper of 20 cm × 8 cm is folded 3 times. Each fold is made along the
line of symmetry, which is perpendicular to its long edge. The perimeter of the final
folded sheet (in cm) is
questions.subtopic: Paper folding, cutting, and patterns in 2 and 3 dimensions
questions.explaination: Starting at $20 \times 8\text{ cm}$, the 1st fold perpendicular to the long edge yields $10 \times 8\text{ cm}$. The 2nd fold perpendicular to the new long edge ($10\text{ cm}$) yields $5 \times 8\text{ cm}$. The 3rd fold perpendicular to the new long edge ($8\text{ cm}$) yields $5 \times 4\text{ cm}$. The perimeter of this final folded sheet is $2(5 + 4) = 18\text{ cm}$.
